data.tagline: An Open-Source Instrument for Metabolic Analysis

data.title: Adopt a Distributed Architecture
data.context: The initial v1.0 proposal had a monolithic design. A senior EE review identified significant risks related to analog signal noise and a lack of real-time processing guarantees on a general-purpose OS.
data.decision: The system will be split into two distinct components: a real-time Sensor Front-End (SFE) microcontroller and a Host Processing Unit (HPU) single-board computer. The SFE is responsible for all time-sensitive data acquisition and initial processing. The HPU is responsible for high-level data logging, user interface, and analysis.
data.consequences: This increases initial hardware complexity but massively de-risks the project by isolating the most critical, time-sensitive tasks onto a dedicated, reliable platform. It allows for parallel development of firmware and software.

data.title: Use C++ with PlatformIO for SFE Firmware
data.context: A modern, memory-safe language like Rust was considered for its robustness. However, the project's primary goal is an accelerated path to a mature product.
data.decision: The SFE firmware will be developed in C++ using the PlatformIO IDE. This leverages the vast and mature ecosystem of existing libraries for sensors and peripherals, and the wider talent pool of experienced embedded C++ developers.
data.consequences: This path has lower R&D friction and allows for faster prototyping. A future migration to Rust is noted as a long-term goal for v2.0.

data.title: Deprecate 'DIY' Term and Adopt Formal Disclaimer
data.context: The term 'DIY' was identified as having a potentially amateur connotation and did not reflect the project's professional standards. It was also an implicit, rather than explicit, liability shield.
data.decision: The 'DIY' tag will be removed from the project name and all official documentation. A formal 'Notice of Non-Commercial & Experimental Status' will be adopted and placed in the README and Project Charter. The project's official public title is 'Project VO2: An Open-Source Instrument'.
data.consequences: This elevates the project's professional branding, making it more attractive to senior talent and potential funders, while providing a stronger, more explicit liability shield.

data.core_principle: A flexible, iterative process with just enough structure to ensure consistency and velocity.

stage_1.purpose: Manages expectations during active development and validation.

stage_2.name: Reference Design
stage_2.purpose: Signals maturity and encourages wider adoption as a proven blueprint.

data.primary_goal: Create a high-fidelity, open-source scientific instrument for personal research and educational use.
data.liability_strategy: Managed via a formal, explicit disclaimer ('Notice of Non-Commercial & Experimental Status'). The project provides a Reference Design, and the end-user is responsible for their own implementation.
data.future_considerations: Potential for grant funding from organizations promoting open-source hardware and scientific tools.
